meta: A Christian look at the false belief that real Christians don’t suffer, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that faith brings a trouble-free life. Prosperity messages that promise health and success. Seeing your suffering as proof you are not a true believer. Comparing your hardships with other Christians’ apparent ease. Feeling betrayed by God when hard times came.
teaches: Scripture says the opposite: all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted. It has been granted to believers not only to believe in Christ but also to suffer for Him. Believers throughout the world undergo the same kinds of suffering. Hebrews describes faithful people who were mistreated and destitute; the world was not worthy of them. Suffering is part of the Christian life, and after a little while, God Himself will restore, strengthen, and establish you.
self_statements: If I were a real Christian, I wouldn’t be going through this.
My suffering proves my faith is fake.
Other Christians don’t suffer like I do.
God promised me an easy life.
Something is wrong with my faith.
Faith should protect me from pain.
errors: Overlooking the suffering of faithful people throughout Scripture.
Comparing your hardships with other Christians’ outward lives.
Calling yourself a fake Christian because you suffer.
Believing faith guarantees a pain-free life.
questions: What does 2 Timothy 3:12 say about godly people?
What has been granted to believers, according to Philippians 1:29?
Are believers around the world suffering too?
Did the people of faith in Hebrews 11 suffer?
Did Jesus promise an easy life?
What does God promise after suffering, according to 1 Peter 5:10?
How might God be with me in my suffering?
truth: Real Christians do suffer. Scripture says godly people will face persecution and hardship, and faithful believers throughout history have suffered. My suffering does not mean my faith is fake. After a little while, the God of all grace will restore, strengthen, and establish me.
hw_questions: What has been granted to believers?
Did the faithful in Hebrews 11 suffer?
Did Jesus promise an easy life?
What does God promise after suffering?
hw_truths: My suffering does not mean my faith is fake.
God will restore, strengthen, and establish me.
The world was not worthy of suffering saints.
log: Each day, write one way I am not alone in my suffering: Jesus, Scripture, or other believers.
name_example: And after Sarah has suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called her to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore her, secure her, strengthen her, and establish her.
actions: and write how faithful people endured hardship.
Learn about one persecuted Christian or church today,
Tell a trusted believer about your suffering,
and ask how they have suffered as a Christian.
Write a short prayer of trust
for each hard thing you are facing.
tracker: One way I am not alone
prayer: Lord Jesus, You suffered, and You told me I would have trouble in this world. Help me reject the lie that real Christians don’t suffer. Strengthen my faith in hard times, remind me that I am not alone, and restore and establish me in Your time. In Your name, Amen.
songs: Weariness can be expressed honestly while asking God for restoration.
Jesus understands suffering and invites people to bring their burdens to Him.
Honest distress can coexist with faith and hope in God.
What a Friend We Have in Jesus
This classic hymn invites direct, honest prayer with the Savior who carries our burdens.
